radiusSource: Radius 1.14 +/- 0.08 Jupiter radii, temperature 936 +66/-63 K and mass 4.1 +1.2/-1.0 Jupiter masses: the Exo-REM fit with a surface-gravity prior to the JWST/MIRI and near-infrared photometry of Malin et al. (2024, arXiv:2408.16843), Table 8: 81,500.9 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. Their fits span 1.0 to 1.14 Jupiter radii and 800 to 1050 K. A model radius: the planet is unresolved. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.
orbitalPeriodSource: Derived: Kepler's third law with the sample's semi-major axis 60.562 au and total mass 1.6495 solar masses, 367.0 years of 365.25 d. Bowler et al. (2020, AJ 159, 63; arXiv:1911.10569): the orbitize! OFTI fit to the literature astrometry, distributed as a posterior of 1,000 samples by whereistheplanet 1.0.1 (post_hd95086b.hdf5). Desgrange et al. (2022) refit the orbit with two newer positions using their own code and publish no posterior; those positions test this orbit instead. Picked with tools/objects/hosted-orbits/posterior-pick.py (src/objects/hd-95086-b/source/orbits/pick.json): highest stored likelihood (ln L -5.65).

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray. No image, colour, map or oblateness of HD 95086 b is measured; only its size, mass and orbit are.
